solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something boring on deck, a sanction for servicemen

indicators.note: in a down-style reading one thing placed on another comes after it, so the boring item is put second

parts.note: a deck of cards is a pack
a drill is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: Sailors aboard ship are punished with some tedious chore on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests tedium, but it means making holes; 'deck' is a pack of cards, not part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack drill is a military punishment in which a soldier marches up and down carrying full kit.

clue.text: Pastry case, but no filling portion

indicators.note: without its filling only the outside of the word remains

explanation.surface: A pastry shell with nothing inside makes a small helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pastry case' reads as one thing, a pie shell, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a part or portion of something, as in a piece of cake.

clue.text: Acclaim actor: judge with fulsomeness capital part involving many lines

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: Effusive praise for a performer and a judge in a city scene full of dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapham Junction is a large railway station in south London, one of the busiest in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a district of London, the capital, whose railway junction has a great many tracks converging.

clue.text: Parent circling 4th of June — note it's the due date

indicators.note: to circle something is to go round it, enclosing it
the fourth letter of the following word is the one taken

parts.note: to drop someone a line is to send a note

explanation.surface: A father marks the fourth of June in his diary as when something is expected.
explanation.walkthrough: '4th of June' looks like a date, fitting the due date, but asks for the fourth letter of June.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the time by which something must be finished, its due date.

clue.text: One succeeding around theatre, flipping amateur!

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, enclosing it
flipping turns something over, so this word runs backwards

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a bungling understudy who has taken over a theatre role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive here, but it signals turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, amateur and inexpert both describe work done without skill.

clue.text: Works progressing slowly in large Greek city

parts.note: Argos is an ancient city in the Peloponnese

explanation.surface: Construction projects in a big Greek city are moving slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' suggests building projects, but means musical pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A largo is a piece or movement played at a very slow tempo.

clue.text: Intimidated fake banking partners getting deals

indicators.note: to bank something is to hold it safely, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: cod as an adjective means sham or mock
West and East are partners at the bridge table, each dealt a hand

explanation.surface: A fraudster frightens business associates into signing contracts.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West; West and East play as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cowed is to be frightened into submission, a direct synonym of intimidated.

clue.text: Reach outside parking, getting learner to drive

indicators.note: one piece sits on the outside of another, wrapping it

parts.note: to reach a place is to come to it
P is the sign for parking
the L-plate for a learner driver

explanation.surface: Arriving at a car park, a learner is allowed to take the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone to act is to force them, the sense of compel.

clue.text: Effect of cool current catchword I'll only half finish off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so these letters are disordered
only half means the second half of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before being halved

explanation.surface: Someone vows to leave a slogan half done, oddly tied to a cool trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool current' reads like a fashionable trend, but means a cold wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind-chill factor measures how much colder moving air makes the temperature feel.

clue.text: One improving property of solution for paparazzo?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who builds on or upgrades land and buildings
second meaning: the chemical bath that brings out a photographic image

explanation.surface: A characteristic of a press photographer's answer, seemingly a way to better oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Property' and 'solution' both look abstract; one is real estate, the other a liquid chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A property developer improves buildings, and photographic developer is the liquid that reveals film images.

clue.text: Issue has article probing Eastern China

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so this piece is pushed inside another

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece investigating the Far East is published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is Cockney rhyming slang for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to issue and to emanate both mean to come out or flow from a source.

clue.text: Signifier of five divided by zero for ruling family

indicators.note: dividing something splits it, and the splitting piece sits in the gap

parts.note: five is written as a Roman V
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A mathematical puzzle about dividing five by nothing, oddly linked to a dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divided by' reads as arithmetic, but it means the zero splits the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romanovs were the dynasty that ruled Russia until the 1917 revolution.

clue.text: Chemist's radical limits of experiment hastily left

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundaries, so take its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rebellious scientist rushes out, abandoning the bounds of an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits of' governs both experiment and hastily.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit; ethyl, C2H5, is one.

clue.text: Established state's Romance language

explanation.surface: A country's official tongue is said to be a Latin-derived one.
explanation.definitionFit: Provençal, the Occitan dialect of southern France, descends from Latin and so is a Romance tongue.

clue.text: Tailor is near my place to learn the cloth trade

definitions.text: place to learn the cloth trade

indicators.note: a tailor cuts and alters material, so these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A tailor says he lives near where people study the textile business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is the clergy, so the cloth trade is the priesthood, not dressmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary trains priests, people who will wear clerical dress, known as the cloth.

clue.text: Slav with yen to devour very mature cheese

indicators.note: devouring takes something inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a Serb is a Slavic person

explanation.surface: A Serbian with a craving gobbles up a well-ripened cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' suggests a longing, fitting the eating picture, but gives the currency letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage Derby is an English cheese marbled green with sage.

clue.text: Speaker's issue — if so, it makes lout pout?

wordplay.words: if so, it makes lout pout
wordplay.note: a lout becomes a pout when its first letter, el, equals pee; read the answer as that statement

explanation.surface: A speech problem that turns a yob into a sulky face.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into three words, letter L, is, letter P; if that held, lout would change into pout.
explanation.definitionFit: A lisp is a speech impediment, an issue affecting how someone talks.

clue.text: Pay off Conservative no longer lying?

parts.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person
someone no longer lying in bed is up

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who has stopped telling untruths settles a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests dishonesty, apt for a politician, but means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is to settle a bill or debt, paying off what is owed.

clue.text: Funny games with copper, one you can't trust

explanation.surface: Something odd about sport involving a police officer who is not trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny in the sense of strange or odd is a synonym of peculiar.

clue.text: Starter of gourmet Polish food

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A first course of fine Polish cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the verb meaning to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for something to eat.

clue.text: Conclude covering Queen — Queen or Supergrass?

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap round it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to seal a deal is to conclude it

explanation.surface: A music question: is the band Queen, or is it Supergrass?
explanation.walkthrough: Queen and Supergrass are both British rock bands; a supergrass is also an informer who betrays many associates.
explanation.definitionFit: A squealer is slang for someone who informs to the police, which a supergrass does on a large scale.

clue.text: Smells not right around opening of insect repellent

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, enclosing it
not means without, so a letter is removed
an opening is the start, so only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: Bad smells near the start of applying bug spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect repellent' reads as one product, but repellent is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Repellent as an adjective means disgusting, a synonym of odious.

clue.text: French booze — idiot thus knocked back bottles

indicators.note: a bottle holds things inside, so one piece contains another
knocked back means sent backwards, so this word runs in reverse

explanation.surface: A fool downs his drinks and then hoards the bottles of French liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking, fitting booze, but signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur from France, used in kir.

clue.text: Firm about boring worthless stuff, a TV genre

indicators.note: about means turned round, so this word is read backwards
something boring drills into another thing, so it sits inside it

parts.note: to stuff is to ram or cram

explanation.surface: A company's tedious rubbish is described as a kind of television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worthless stuff' looks like one noun phrase, but it splits: worthless is a dud, and stuff is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A docudrama is a dramatised documentary, a recognised kind of television programme.

clue.text: You heard holy man from the east displays taste

indicators.note: what is heard is a sound, so the letter that sounds like the word is used

parts.note: the letter U sounds like you

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: an imam leads prayers in a mosque

explanation.surface: A holy man arriving from the East shows refined discernment.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth basic taste, alongside sweet, sour, salt and bitter.

clue.text: Still pirouetting in Montmartre nightspot

indicators.note: a pirouette spins round, so the letters are turned back
in means the letters lie within the following words

explanation.surface: A dancer is still spinning in a Paris cabaret club.
explanation.walkthrough: Montmartre's nightspots include the Moulin Rouge, so pirouetting fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Still as an adjective means motionless, and inert means not moving.

clue.text: Game, I sense, is draining for the finances

explanation.surface: Someone decides a pursuit is costing too much money.
explanation.walkthrough: Nous is British informal for practical good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous means bringing financial ruin, so it describes something extremely costly.

clue.text: Architrave from which to efface unknown letter

indicators.note: to efface is to rub out, so something is removed from the word

parts.note: the epistyle is the architrave, the beam resting on columns
algebraic unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: Instructions on a building site to remove an anonymous mark from a classical beam.
explanation.walkthrough: Epistyle is the Greek-derived name for the architrave of a classical building.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, such as those of the New Testament.

clue.text: Media group pocketing no returns for ages

indicators.note: something that returns comes back, so the whole is read backwards
to pocket something is to put it inside, so one piece is held within another

explanation.surface: A broadcaster keeps cashing in without giving anything back for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Yonks is British slang for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks means a long time, as in 'I haven't seen her for yonks'.

clue.text: Outstanding person who sings, a real prima donna!

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing, and a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: A star singer is praised as truly temperamental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person who sings' suggests an opera star to match prima donna, but it means an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A superbrat is a spoilt, tantrum-prone star, especially a tennis player, so a real diva.
